chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while he was absent and bore witness to her divorce, then he returned and stayed with the woman for months and did not inform her of her divorce. Then the woman claimed pregnancy, so the man said, 'I have divorced you and I bore witness to your divorce.' He (the Imam) said, 'The child is attributed to him, and his word is not accepted.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man divorces his wife while absent, returns, lives with her, and then disputes her pregnancy?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in Shia jurisprudence, where the marriage bond is presumed to remain intact until proven otherwise. The Imam’s ruling that the child is attributed to the husband and his prior divorce claim is rejected highlights the evidentiary weight of cohabitation and the protection of lineage (*nasab*) when a spouse is unaware of the divorce.
